title: MCPTool
description: The MCP WIRE PROJECTION of a tool — exactly what appears in an MCP `tools/list` response. This is a strict subset of the ToolSpec IR (events/v1/tool-spec.schema.json), and the difference is the point: side_effect, trust_required, rate limits and audit flags are L.I.O.N.E.L's authorization metadata and MUST NOT leave the system. Emitting them would tell a remote peer exactly which tool is the soft target.

compatibility.notes: Field names use MCP's camelCase `inputSchema`, NOT our snake_case — this schema describes someone else's wire format and must match it exactly. That inconsistency with the rest of contracts/ is deliberate and should not be 'fixed'. This is a PROJECTION, not a second source of truth: ToolSpec remains authoritative and MCPTool is derived from it. Never author an MCPTool by hand.

inputSchema.description: MCP spells this camelCase. Constrained to the same portable JSON Schema subset as ToolSpec — no oneOf/anyOf/allOf, because that is where provider support diverges.

annotations.description: MCP's optional behavioural hints. HINTS ONLY — never a security control. `readOnlyHint` is a courtesy to the client, not a substitute for the Policy Engine's side_effect check (ADR-0012), which runs regardless of what a remote server claims about itself.

examples.name: system.get_disk_usage
examples.title: Disk usage
examples.description: Report free and total disk space for a mounted volume on this machine. Use when the user asks about storage, free space, or whether something will fit. Does not delete or move anything.
